tracks.title: Product and domain
tracks.objective: Confirm that terminology, lifecycle, ownership and user-visible scenarios match the intended Dirizhor operating model.
questions: Are the user, decision owner, Director and AI responsibilities unambiguous?
Do the lifecycle states cover the confirmed MVP scenarios without hidden business decisions?
Are corporate memory provenance, replacement and retention semantics understandable?
completion_requirements: Record contradictions, missing decisions and terminology findings with exact locations.
Confirm that every blocking or major domain finding has an owner and disposition.
Attach an opaque ticket or artifact reference to the completed track.

tracks.title: Application and API
tracks.objective: Verify that HTTP contracts, state transitions, errors and Director-Gateway interactions are mutually consistent.
questions: Do prose, OpenAPI and reference handlers define the same request, response and error contracts?
Are idempotency, pagination, concurrency and confirmation transitions fail-closed?
Can any public or internal route bypass the declared module boundary?
completion_requirements: Trace at least one read-only and one mutating MVP flow across API boundaries.
Record every contract mismatch with an exact operation or schema location.
Attach an opaque ticket or artifact reference to the completed track.

tracks.title: Security
tracks.objective: Challenge authentication, authorization, confirmation, audit and service trust boundaries for bypasses and unsafe defaults.
questions: Can UI, AI, Gateway, operator or a service identity bypass deny, RBAC, confirmation or audit?
Are browser, workload-token, mTLS and secret boundaries independent and fail-closed?
Do rotation, revocation, replay and target canaries prove the stated controls?
completion_requirements: Review every open security finding and identify required target evidence.
Classify authorization, confidentiality or integrity ambiguity as blocking.
Attach an opaque ticket or artifact reference to the completed track.

tracks.title: Data and recovery
tracks.objective: Verify persistence, migration, privilege, backup and recovery contracts against the declared data model.
questions: Do logical ownership, SQL constraints and API lifecycle rules agree?
Are expand, backfill, validate, contract and rollback paths executable without runtime DDL rights?
Can backup, PITR and logical restore meet the proposed RPO and RTO with verifiable evidence?
completion_requirements: Review migration history, runtime privilege and restore evidence requirements.
Record any data-loss, corruption or unrecoverable migration risk as blocking.
Attach an opaque ticket or artifact reference to the completed track.

tracks.title: Platform and SRE
tracks.objective: Assess deployability, observability, failure isolation, recovery, rollback and operational adoption decisions.
questions: Are rollout order, probes, stop-ship criteria and rollback ownership explicit?
Are SLO, outage budget, RPO, RTO, retention and alert thresholds mutually consistent?
Does every production-readiness claim have target-specific, independently reviewable evidence?
completion_requirements: Review all NOT_RUN target checks and adoption decision placeholders.
Identify the owner and evidence source for each accepted operational risk.
Attach an opaque ticket or artifact reference to the completed track.

tracks.title: Engineering implementation
tracks.objective: Confirm that reference code, tests, build artifacts and evidence tooling implement the published specifications without hidden dependencies.
questions: Do implementation and tests enforce the architecture guardrails at runtime boundaries?
Are build and release results reproducible from the exact reviewed Git baseline?
Can evidence tooling be bypassed by dirty sources, ignored private files or artifact drift?
completion_requirements: Verify release evidence and source/build matches for the exact baseline.
Record untested shared behavior, hidden workspace dependency or evidence gap.
Attach an opaque ticket or artifact reference to the completed track.
